Pembina Pipeline (TSX:PPL)

Overview: Pembina Pipeline is a Calgary based energy infrastructure company that moves and processes oil sands crude, natural gas and liquids across North America.

Operations: Pembina Pipeline generates about CA$3.4b from Pipelines, CA$1.3b from Facilities, and CA$4.7b from Marketing & New Ventures, partly offset by CA$1.1b of corporate eliminations.

Market Cap: CA$41.1b

Pembina Pipeline matters for this Canadian Oil Sands Upstream Producers screen because its pipes, processing assets and export links sit where rising oil sands volumes, LNG build out and Asian demand all converge. This is exactly what the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St focuses on.

Athabasca Oil (TSX:ATH)

Overview: Athabasca Oil is a Calgary based producer focused on Alberta thermal oil sands and light oil, tightly linked to bitumen economics.

Operations: Athabasca Oil generates about CA$1.4b from its Athabasca thermal oil unit and CA$116.6 million from Duvernay Energy, almost entirely in Canada.

Market Cap: CA$5.5b

Athabasca Oil is one of the purest plays on the Canadian Oil Sands Upstream Producers theme, with thermal projects and bitumen focused assets that plug directly into royalty policy, export access and LNG linked demand shifts highlighted in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St.

data.title: Missed Exelixis's Run? What Holders Had To Believe
data.description:
If you had bought Exelixis on 19 November 2025 and simply sat tight, the outcome would look very different today. Holding Exelixis over the past year would have returned 57.6%, including dividends. That headline invites a harder question. At the time, you were staring at an oncology specialist tied closely to cabozantinib, rising 340B pressure, and an unproven zanzalintinib franchise. If you were weighing that decision then, how much conviction could you really have in Exelixis becoming more than a single-drug story?

Exelixis has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 36 healthcare AI stocks.

The Two Exelixis Stories Investors Were Arguing About

The shares cost US$42.14 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at Exelixis then had to choose between a growth script powered by oncology demand and a much more cautious pricing and regulation story.

On the bullish side, the optimistic narrative saw a Fair Value of US$60, a price implied by expectations that a broader oncology portfolio could justify it. Supporters leaned on assumptions that zanzalintinib might eventually eclipse the cabozantinib franchise in high value, lower competition indications.

The bearish narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$36, again an implied price based on its own set of forecasts. This camp focused on the risk that rising 340B volume near 24% and tighter drug price scrutiny could compress margins even if cabozantinib demand held up.

What The Results Changed In The Exelixis Debate

Exelixis kept cabozantinib at the center of the story, with Q3 2026 revenue of US$658.7 million and net income of US$218.1 million, which supported the optimistic script that the core franchise could still pull higher profit and a slightly stronger 33.1% margin. The extension of the FDA review for zanzalintinib to March 2027 gave the cautious case fresh support. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The real lesson is where to point your flashlight. When a single product carries most of the load, track both revenue mix and net margin alongside every big regulatory date. That is how you test whether a diversification story at another biotech is actually progressing or just being talked about.

What Exelixis Buyers Are Assuming After The Run

Exelixis now trades at US$65.83. The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St views its Fair Value as below that quote, framing today’s price as already baking in meaningful success from cabozantinib cash generation and a broader oncology pipeline.

The same Narrative argues that for this level to hold, investors must judge that cabozantinib strength, disciplined R&D and the zanzalintinib program together can support a durable multi asset oncology model without leaving earnings overly exposed to execution slips.

data.description:

  • The US Commerce Department has reportedly approved large scale sales of AMD AI chips into China under current export rules.

data.title: What ASML Doubters Overlooked
data.description:
If ASML sat on your watchlist instead of in your portfolio, the gain over the last year may feel like a missed shot. Holding ASML over the past year would have returned 40.9%, including dividends. That outcome raises a sharper question. Back on 20 November 2025, when analysts still argued over how fast EUV and High NA tools might spread, what signals could have helped you judge whether AI driven wafer starts would really justify those bullish adoption assumptions?

ASML has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On ASML

The shares cost €890 at the start of the period. At that point, ASML sat between two very different stories about how deep the AI driven wafer cycle might run and how much lithography spending governments and chipmakers would really commit to.

On the bullish side, one narrative saw a Fair Value of €950, a price implied by expectations that AI, cloud and data center demand would drive EUV and High NA tools, plus service contracts, far beyond prior cycles. That view leaned on an assumption that earnings could reach €13.9b by about 2028 with P/E at 31.6x.

The more cautious script pinned Fair Value at €769, a level based on assumed revenue growth of 7.2% and profit margin of 30.4% over roughly three years. It treated geopolitical risk and export controls as central threats, with tariffs and restrictions on China seen as potential brakes on ASML’s addressable market and High NA adoption.

What The Results Changed For The ASML Thesis

Record Q3 2026 figures gave the bullish ASML story its strongest support. Reported revenue reached €11.7b versus €7.5b a year earlier, and net income moved from €2.1b to €5.0b. Net margin shifted from 28.3% to 42.5%. Management also reported demand for AI related tools that supply cannot fully match. Rising export control risk around China still challenged the upside case, so the evidence cut both ways.

The whole debate turned on how much AI driven lithography demand would show up in actual orders and profitability. For any other chip equipment group, the same check is simple. Track multi quarter revenue, backlog comments and reported net margin against the story being told about AI and wafer starts.

What ASML’s Run Leaves You Paying For Today

ASML now trades at €1,168 after a 40.9% gain over the past year, and this Narrative’s Fair Value view sits below that level. The gap reflects concern that today’s quote already charges a premium for ASML’s position in advanced lithography.

According to Thomas_Regrettier, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, the crux for anyone buying at today’s price is whether ASML can keep its geopolitical exposure contained while remaining the dominant supplier of leading edge tools to a very small group of customers.

"ASML’s story is one of quiet dominance at the heart of global tech. Founded in the Netherlands in 1984, ASML started as a joint venture between Philips and ASM International. Over the decades, it evolved into the sole supplier in the world of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are essential for manufacturing the most advanced semiconductor chips (like those powering AI, smartphones, and data centers)."

data.title: Is It Smart To Buy Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) Before It Goes Ex-Dividend?
data.description:
Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) stock is about to trade ex-dividend in three days. The ex-dividend date is usually set to be one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. The ex-dividend date is important because any transaction on a stock needs to have been settled before the record date in order to be eligible for a dividend. Therefore, if you purchase Xylem's shares on or after the 24th of November, you won't be eligible to receive the dividend, when it is paid on the 22nd of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.43 per share. Last year, in total, the company distributed US$1.72 to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that Xylem has a trailing yield of 1.8% on the current share price of US$95.24. Dividends are a major contributor to investment returns for long term holders, but only if the dividend continues to be paid. So we need to check whether the dividend payments are covered, and if earnings are growing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are typically paid out of company income, so if a company pays out more than it earned, its dividend is usually at a higher risk of being cut. That's why it's good to see Xylem paying out a modest 37% of its earnings. A useful secondary check can be to evaluate whether Xylem generated enough free cash flow to afford its dividend. Fortunately, it paid out only 44% of its free cash flow in the past year.

It's positive to see that Xylem's dividend is covered by both profits and cash flow, since this is generally a sign that the dividend is sustainable, and a lower payout ratio usually suggests a greater margin of safety before the dividend gets cut.

Check out our latest analysis for Xylem

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Companies with consistently growing earnings per share generally make the best dividend stocks, as they usually find it easier to grow dividends per share. If business enters a downturn and the dividend is cut, the company could see its value fall precipitously. It's encouraging to see Xylem has grown its earnings rapidly, up 27% a year for the past five years. Earnings per share have been growing very quickly, and the company is paying out a relatively low percentage of its profit and cash flow. Companies with growing earnings and low payout ratios are often the best long-term dividend stocks, as the company can both grow its earnings and increase the percentage of earnings that it pays out, essentially multiplying the dividend.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. Xylem has delivered an average of 11% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past 10 years of dividend payments. Both per-share earnings and dividends have both been growing rapidly in recent times, which is great to see.

The Bottom Line

Is Xylem an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? We love that Xylem is growing earnings per share while simultaneously paying out a low percentage of both its earnings and cash flow. These characteristics suggest the company is reinvesting in growing its business, while the conservative payout ratio also implies a reduced risk of the dividend being cut in the future. It's a promising combination that should mark this company worthy of closer attention.

data.title: Earnings Release: Here's Why Analysts Cut Their Super League Enterprise, Inc. (NASDAQ:SLE) Price Target To US$10.67
data.description:
Shareholders might have noticed that Super League Enterprise, Inc. (NASDAQ:SLE) filed its quarterly result this time last week. The early response was not positive, with shares down 9.8% to US$3.58 in the past week. Revenues of US$2.6m missed forecasts by 15%, but at least statutory losses were much smaller than expected, with per-share losses of US$0.83 coming in 48% smaller than what the analysts had forecast. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on Super League Enterprise after the latest results.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Super League Enterprise's three analysts is for revenues of US$18.5m in 2027. This reflects a huge 57% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. The loss per share is expected to greatly reduce in the near future, narrowing 62% to US$3.91. Before this latest report, the consensus had been expecting revenues of US$18.7m and US$4.52 per share in losses. While the revenue estimates were largely unchanged, sentiment seems to have improved, with the analysts upgrading their numbers and making a cut to losses per share in particular.

See our latest analysis for Super League Enterprise

The consensus price target fell 8.6% to US$10.67despite the forecast for smaller losses next year. It looks like the ongoing lack of profitability is starting to weigh on valuations. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. The most optimistic Super League Enterprise analyst has a price target of US$14.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$6.00. Note the wide gap in analyst price targets? This implies to us that there is a fairly broad range of possible scenarios for the underlying business.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. One thing stands out from these estimates, which is that Super League Enterprise is forecast to grow faster in the future than it has in the past, with revenues expected to display 43% annualised growth until the end of 2027. If achieved, this would be a much better result than the 3.7% annual decline over the past five years. Compare this against analyst estimates for the broader industry, which suggest that (in aggregate) industry revenues are expected to grow 18% annually. So it looks like Super League Enterprise is expected to grow faster than its competitors, at least for a while.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that the analysts made no changes to their forecasts for a loss next year. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of Super League Enterprise's future valuation.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for Super League Enterprise going out to 2027, and you can see them free on our platform here..

We don't want to rain on the parade too much, but we did also find 4 warning signs for Super League Enterprise (2 can't be ignored!) that you need to be mindful of.

data.title: What Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Doubters Got Wrong
data.description:
Regeneron Pharmaceuticals spent this past year stacking fresh deals and clinical milestones, from the Telix radiopharmaceutical tie‑up to FDA approval of Livsayis for generalized myasthenia gravis. Investors who held Regeneron Pharmaceuticals over the past year are up 25.9%, including dividends. If you were deciding whether to buy on 19 November 2025, you would have seen that bullish and bearish analysts were 31% apart on fair value. Which story about Regeneron’s future did that spread really require you to accept?

This theme extends beyond Regeneron Pharmaceuticals. See which of 36 healthcare AI stocks may still merit a closer look.

The Two Stories Regeneron Investors Were Choosing Between

The shares cost US$703 at the start of the period, so anyone looking at Regeneron Pharmaceuticals then had to decide which of two very different stories to lean toward.

On the upbeat side, the bullish camp saw a Fair Value of US$921, a price implied by assumptions that Dupixent and EYLEA HD could capture far greater US and global market share. That view rested on expectations of 7.9% annual revenue growth and rising profit margins, helped by manufacturing expansion and a broader oncology and hematology portfolio.

The bearish narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$540, a level based on the idea that biosimilars and US healthcare reforms would steadily erode pricing power. That scenario assumed revenue growth of only 1.4% a year and profit margins falling to 22.5%, with EYLEA and Dupixent exposure, rising R&D costs, and demographic shifts all pressuring future earnings.

What The Evidence Around Regeneron Actually Tested

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals secured FDA approval for Livsayis in generalized myasthenia gravis and reported Q3 2026 revenue of US$5,115.8m and net income of US$1,948.7m, both above Q3 2025 levels, which leaned toward the bullish growth story. Net margin slipped from 38.9% to 38.1%, and the failed melanoma trial with resulting class actions pushed back against the idea of steadily rising profitability. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key assumption investors were really testing was whether product and partnership wins outpace pricing and pipeline setbacks. For another healthcare stock, you would track whether new approvals, trial readouts, and deal flow show up in higher sales and stable or improving net margin, rather than just in headlines.

What Regeneron’s Current Price Already Assumes

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals now trades at US$923 after a 25.9% gain over the past year. The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St places its Fair Value below that level, even while accepting strong recent execution across Dupixent, EYLEA HD and newer programs.

That Narrative hinges on whether fresh franchises and pipeline assets genuinely offset pricing, trial and legal pressures. A buyer at today’s price effectively assumes the current breadth of commercial performance and late stage drugs holds up. The question is how those risks affect that belief in durability.

"The main factor that has to go right is that Regeneron Pharmaceuticals converts its broad pipeline and newer franchises such as EYLEA HD, Libtayo, cemdisiran and Pasatru into durable earnings streams that offset pricing pressure and legal and regulatory risks."

One Narrative has put a figure on that disagreement. → See the Narrative with its lower Fair Value, assumptions and all

Another Healthcare Story Nearby

Regeneron keeps the focus on drug pipelines and trial readouts. Your next question is where similar pressures are playing out differently.

One large peer is also leaning harder into oncology, immunology and neuroscience. Management there is trying to tilt toward higher margin specialty treatments.

That same group is reshaping its medical device arm and carving out slower pieces. It is spending heavily on early stage deals that currently weigh on reported earnings.

The bet is that these therapies and platforms eventually justify that upfront hit. If the mix shift works, this could be a very different healthcare story to examine.
